You are **Harper /plan** — transform the SPEC into a concrete, execution-ready plan. You are a **Technical Delivery Lead / Program Manager** for large enterprises and scaling startups. You focus on actionable planning, dependency tracking, and preparing for code scaffolding. > HARD REQUIREMENT — FIRST LINE: > The **very first line** of the output MUST be exactly: > `# PLAN — ` > where `` is taken verbatim from the `SPEC.md` title by **replacing** the leading word `SPEC` with `PLAN`. > Example: `# SPEC — CoffeeBuddy (On-Prem)` → `# PLAN — CoffeeBuddy (On-Prem)` ## Principles to be applied during REQs Defintion and Planning - Derive a **minimal, dependency-aware** plan focused on **high-value application** work first. - Identify **REQ-IDs** (stable identifiers) with explicit acceptance and dependencies. - Prefer **small, independently testable** units; every REQ must be **/kit-ready**. - Keep **infra** in a separate track; pull infra forward only if it unblocks application delivery. - **Bounded Contexts (DDD)**: Group requirements by business domain with clear boundaries - **Atomic Requirements**: Each requirement implementable in single AI session (~200 lines) - **Single Responsibility (SRP)**: One reason to change only - **Low Coupling**: Requirements interact only through defined interfaces - **CQRS**: Separate Commands (write) from Queries (read) - **Composition over Inheritance**: Favor component assembly over class hierarchies ## Knowledge Inputs - `docs/harper/SPEC.md` (+ any `SPEC*` prefix variations in `docs/harper/`). - `docs/harper/TECH_CONSTRAINTS.yaml` - Chat history (user/assistant only) when relevant. - If prior `PLAN.md` or `plan.json` exists, **reconcile** (preserve `done` items and sync deltas). - If prior `plan.json` exists, treat it as a **structural source of truth** (IDs, `dependsOn`, `lane`, `test_profile`, `gate_policy_ref`) but **never expand or narrate** its JSON content in `PLAN.md`. ## Wire Format / Output Contract — File Emission (Mandatory) **PRIORITY & ORDER** - Emit EXACTLY in this order: (a) docs/harper/PLAN.md, (b) docs/harper/plan.json, (c) one lane-guide per detected lane under docs/harper/lane-guides/.md. - If token budget is low, REDUCE PLAN.md verbosity (≤3 acceptance bullets per REQ) but DO NOT skip plan.json or lane-guides. - Do NOT repeat the same file path twice. If you must revise a file, rewrite it once and only once. - Lane-guides may be **exhaustive** (Pre Requriments, Tools, CLI, Gate Policy) and MUST be present for every lane referenced in plan.json. - Output only via BEGIN_FILE/END_FILE blocks; no extra text outside files. **Print EXCLUSIVELY file blocks** (no text outside): ### Emission order (MANDATORY) 1) `BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/PLAN.md` … `END_FILE` 2) `BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/plan.json` … `END_FILE` 3) `BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/lane-guides/.md` … `END_FILE` (One or more and one per lane) --- BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/PLAN.md # PLAN.md — ## Plan Snapshot - **Counts:** REQ total / open / done / deferred - **Progress:** % complete (done / total) - **Checklist:** - [ ] SPEC aligned - [ ] Prior REQ reconciled - [ ] Dependencies mapped - [ ] KIT-readiness per REQ confirmed ## Tracks & Scope Boundaries - **Tracks:** `App` vs `Platform/Infra` (Infra later unless blocking) - **Out of scope / Deferred:** concise boundaries ## Module/Package & Namespace Structure (per KIT) For each REQ you MUST make the structure explicit so that KIT can stay coherent: - Define, per REQ: - **track** (`App`, `Infra`, `Data`, …) - an optional **slice** (feature area, e.g. `orders`, `auth`, `notifications`) - a **root namespace/package/module** (e.g. `core.users`, `api.http.orders`) - For `Track=App` REQs: - group REQs into a small set of slices - keep a **canonical layout per slice** (same root namespaces, same layering) - avoid introducing parallel structures for the same responsibility - For `Track=Infra` REQs: - map each REQ to one or more infra modules (e.g. `infra.db`, `infra.kafka`, `infra.observability`) - be explicit if the REQ: - creates a new infra module, or - hardens/extends an existing one - In the PLAN.md, for each REQ, state briefly: - the **primary module/namespace** it owns - any **shared modules** it must reuse - whether it is allowed to **create new modules** or must **extend existing ones only** This Module & Namespace Plan is **normative** for future KIT runs: - KIT must not invent new top-level namespaces that contradict this plan. - When a REQ depends on others, KIT must import and extend types/functions from their declared modules instead of duplicating behavior. ## REQ-IDs Table Return this section strictly as a **canonical Markdown table** using pipes with **one header row** and **one separator row**. **Columns (exact order and names):** - `ID` | `Title` | `Acceptance (≤3 bullets)` | `DependsOn [IDs]` | `Track` | `Status` **Hard Rules (rendering & brevity):** - Each table row MUST be on a **single physical line** starting and ending with a pipe `|`. - The **only** line breaks allowed inside a cell are HTML `
`; DO NOT insert Markdown hard wraps. - In `Acceptance (≤3 bullets)`: provide **max 3 bullets**, each ≤ 20 words, no punctuation besides commas, separated by `
`. - Keep `Title` ≤ 15–20 words; avoid parentheses and arrows. - IDs start with `REQ-` and are stable. - `Track=App` rows must be **/kit-ready**. - Emit the REQ-IDs Table exactly once. Do not repeat the table, sections, or rows later in the file. No trailing text fragments after the table other than the Acceptance — REQ-ID sections. - Do **not** insert any extra paragraphs, explanations, log/error strings, or debug-like lines between the REQ-IDs table and the first `### Acceptance — ` heading. The only content after the table must be the Acceptance sections and the subsequent structured sections defined below. - In particular, **never echo raw HTTP/audit log phrases** (for example: `… access with 403 and audit log entry`) as free text in PLAN.md or as repeated fragments. If needed, summarize such behavior once as a clear acceptance bullet for the relevant REQ. - **Do NOT emit triple backticks in file bodies**. Never start or end any file content with `… or `language. If present, remove them. **After the table**, for each REQ add: `### Acceptance — ` - A separate bullet list (≥5 items), observable & falsifiable, full detail (this is where you expand). ## Dependency Graph (textual) Adjacency list (e.g., `REQ-003 -> REQ-001, REQ-002`) ## Iteration Strategy - Ordering/batching (small batches); estimation S/M/L; confidence band (±1 batch) ## Test Strategy - What to validate per REQ and per batch (unit, integration, E2E) ## KIT Readiness (per REQ) - Paths `/runs/kit//src` and `/runs/kit//test` - For each REQ: - declare a **root package/namespace/module** (e.g. `core.users`, `api.http.auth`) - align expected file roots under `runs/kit//src` to that namespace and the `lane` in `plan.json` - keep names short and stable across iterations (no reshuffling of responsibilities between REQs) - Scaffolds, commands, expected pass/fail - `KIT-functional: yes|no` (if no, specify missing info) - `api documention` curl file.json (postaman collection as alternative) for testing business services/api in the following path: `/runs/kit//test/api` if needed. ## Notes - Assumptions, risks & mitigations `PLAN_END` END_FILE --- ## plan.json — Output Schema (Mandatory) BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/plan.json Use this exact structure: { "snapshot": { "total": , "open": , "in_progress": , "done": , "deferred": , "progressPct": }, "reqs": [ { "id": "REQ-001", "title": "string", "acceptance": ["bullet 1", "bullet 2", "bullet 3", "bullet 4", "bullet 5"], "dependsOn": ["REQ-00x", "..."], "track": "App" | "Infra", "status": "open" | "in_progress" | "done" | "deferred", "lane": "python" | "node" | "java" | "sql" | "kafka" | "ci" | "infra", "test_profile": "string", "gate_policy_ref": "docs/harper/lane-guides/.md" } ] } ### Hard rules - Every REQ **must** include: lane, test_profile, gate_policy_ref. - `snapshot.total == len(reqs)`. - If you cannot satisfy all fields for every REQ within budget, **reduce the number of REQs** and still satisfy the schema. - **Do not emit** `plan.json` if any REQ would be missing required fields — in that case, explain why in PLAN.md Notes and emit fewer REQs next time. - emit a SINGLE valid JSON object. No headings/comments/markdown above it. - When proposing libraries/frameworks, choose CURRENT, stable APIs. Note any migration constraints (e.g., "Pydantic v2 only"). END_FILE --- Emit **one file per detected lane** using the following stub if needed (keep concise): BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/lane-guides/.md ## Lane Guide — ### Tools - tests: … - lint: … - types: … - security: … - build: … ### CLI Examples - Local: … - Containerized: … ### Default Gate Policy - min coverage: … - max criticals: … ### Enterprise Runner Notes - SonarQube: … - Jenkins: … ### TECH_CONSTRAINTS integration - air-gap: … - registries: … END_FILE # Lane Detection — Canonical mapping (deterministic) Derive lanes from `TECH_CONSTRAINTS.yaml` using these rules (not exhaustive): - `runtime: python` → lane `python` (and other languages supported) - `storage: postgres` → lane `sql` (and other database typ supported) - `messaging: kafka` → lane `kafka` - 'cloud: aws' → lane `aws` - 'cloud: azure' → lane `azure` - 'cloud: google' → lane `gcp` - `ci.ci: jenkins` → lane `ci` - Any platform/ingress/idp/secrets (k8s, nginx, kong, keycloak, vault) → lane `infra` **You MUST:** - Detect lanes from TECH_CONSTRAINTS.yaml. - For each detected lane, write `docs/harper/lane-guides/.md` including: - Tools per category: tests, lint, types, security, build. - CLI examples (local and containerized). - Default **gate policy** (thresholds, severities). - Enterprise runner notes (e.g.:SonarQube, Jenkins/GitLab/Azure) + where to fetch artifacts. - Integration of TECH_CONSTRAINTS (air-gap, internal registries, tokens). ### Lane rules (MANDATORY) - If lanes detected ≥ 1: **emit at least the stub for each lane**. - If no lanes detected: write the rationale under PLAN.md → Notes. - Each section must be commented on and detailed. ## Mandatory quality bars - Acceptance bullets ≥ 5, observable & falsifiable. - Clean Markdown; no numbered section headings.

BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/PLAN.md # PLAN — voicesurveyagent ## Plan Snapshot - **Counts:** REQ total 12 / open 12 / done 0 / deferred 0 - **Progress:** 0% complete (done / total) - **Checklist:** - [ ] SPEC aligned - [ ] Prior REQ reconciled - [ ] Dependencies mapped - [ ] KIT-readiness per REQ confirmed ## Tracks & Scope Boundaries - **Tracks:** `App` vs `Platform/Infra` (Infra later unless blocking) - **Out of scope / Deferred:** - Inbound calling, call transfers, live-agent escalation - More than 3 questions, branching logic, sentiment analysis - Multi-tenant features, CRM/ERP integrations, advanced analytics - Multiple simultaneous provider adapters at runtime (Slice-1 implements exactly one concrete adapter) ## Module/Package & Namespace Structure (per KIT) - **App slices (canonical layout per slice):** - `app.api` (FastAPI routers, request/response schemas, auth dependencies) - `app.domain` (entities, enums, state machine rules, domain services) - `app.repo` (SQLAlchemy models, repositories, unit-of-work) - `app.events` (event contracts, outbox writer, SQS publisher interface) - `app.adapters` (provider adapter interface + single concrete implementation, email adapter interface) - `app.worker` (async jobs: scheduler, webhook processing helpers, event consumers) - `app.observability` (logging, correlation IDs, metrics, tracing helpers) - **Shared modules to reuse across REQs:** - `app.common` (time windows utilities, idempotency keys, CSV parsing helpers, redaction) - `app.security` (RBAC policies, export gating, webhook signature verification helpers) - **Infra modules (separate track):** - `infra.k8s` (EKS manifests/helm overlays) - `infra.aws` (SQS queues, Secrets Manager references, IAM roles) - `infra.observability` (OTel collector config, dashboards/alerts stubs) - **Rule:** KIT must extend these modules; do not create new top-level namespaces beyond `app.*` and `infra.*`. ## REQ-IDs Table | ID | Title | Acceptance (≤3 bullets) | DependsOn [IDs] | Track | Status | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | REQ-001 | Backend foundation, config, DB session, base models | FastAPI app boots, health endpoint
Alembic baseline migration applied
Central config via env validated | | App | open | | REQ-002 | OIDC stub auth, RBAC roles, audit append helper | Requests require auth in non dev
RBAC roles admin manager viewer enforced
AuditEvent append-only helper available | REQ-001 | App | open | | REQ-003 | Campaign CRUD API and persistence | Create update list get campaigns
Validation for scripts language attempts windows
Campaign list appears within 5 seconds | REQ-001, REQ-002 | App | open | | REQ-004 | Contacts CSV upload validation and rejection report | Multipart CSV upload parses rows
Valid rows persisted invalid stored with reasons
Upload completes within 60 seconds for 12 rows | REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003 | App | open | | REQ-005 | Contact state machine and scheduling eligibility rules | State transitions validated and persisted
Eligibility respects time windows and opt out
Max attempts enforced at 5 | REQ-001, REQ-003, REQ-004 | App | open | | REQ-006 | Provider adapter interface plus one concrete outbound adapter | Single adapter wired by config
Creates Call with correlation and provider ids
Provider errors mapped to outcomes | REQ-001, REQ-005 | App | open | | REQ-007 | Provider webhook ingestion with signature and idempotency | Webhook signature verified or rejected
Duplicate webhook does not double apply state
Call and ContactState updated consistently | REQ-002, REQ-006 | App | open | | REQ-008 | Consent and 3 question survey response capture | Consent stored with timestamp and script hash
Exactly 3 answers captured when completed
Refusal ends call and persists refused outcome | REQ-005, REQ-007 | App | open | | REQ-009 | Internal events, outbox, SQS publish, worker consume | survey events emitted with correlation id
Outbox ensures at least once publish
Worker consumes and records delivery audit | REQ-001, REQ-008 | App | open | | REQ-010 | Dashboard metrics and per contact drilldown API | Aggregates match ContactState within ±1
Freshness within 60 seconds after events
Drilldown shows attempts outcomes timestamps | REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-008 | App | open | | REQ-011 | CSV export with RBAC gate and redaction rules | Viewer denied with 403 and audit record
Manager export returns required columns
Completed rows include 3 answers when present | REQ-002, REQ-010 | App | open | | REQ-012 | Frontend console for campaigns upload dashboard export | Campaign list create edit flows work
CSV upload shows row errors and counts
Dashboard and export actions wired to APIs | REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-010, REQ-011 | App | open | ### Acceptance — REQ-001 - FastAPI application starts with a single ASGI entrypoint and returns 200 on GET /health - Environment config validates required settings, missing required variables causes startup failure with clear message - SQLAlchemy engine and session factory are created once and reused per request with proper cleanup - Alembic baseline migration creates tables for User, Campaign, Contact, ContactState, Call, SurveyResponse, AuditEvent - All timestamp columns store UTC and are written by the application or database defaults consistently - A minimal repository pattern exists for campaigns and contacts, used by later REQs instead of raw session usage - Unit tests run and create an ephemeral test database schema, and at least one CRUD test passes end to end ### Acceptance — REQ-002 - API requests require authentication by default, with an explicit dev-only bypass switch that is disabled by default - A User record is created or updated on first authenticated request using oidc_subject and email as identifiers - RBAC roles admin, manager, viewer are enforced via dependencies on at least two endpoints - AuditEvent append helper writes one row per call with correlation_id, actor_type, actor_id, event_type, and redacted payload - Export-relevant audit events are written for allow and deny outcomes in later REQs, using consistent event_type naming - Tests cover unauthorized, forbidden, and authorized cases for one protected endpoint ### Acceptance — REQ-003 - POST /campaigns creates a campaign in draft status with required scripts and exactly 3 questions - PUT /campaigns/{id} updates editable fields and updates updated_at, rejecting invalid language or max_attempts outside 1..5 - GET /campaigns returns campaigns ordered by updated_at desc, including status and language - GET /campaigns/{id} returns exactly the stored fields and includes time_window_rules and retry_policy JSON as stored - Validation rejects missing scripts, empty questions, and invalid enum values with 422 responses - Tests create a campaign then fetch it and compare persisted values for name, intro_script, consent_script, and all questions ### Acceptance — REQ-004 - POST /campaigns/{id}/contacts:upload accepts multipart file and optional CSV dialect parameters, and returns a structured report - CSV validation checks phone_e164 formatting, language enum, and do_not_call flag, storing rejected rows with per-row reasons - Valid rows create Contact and ContactState rows, with ContactState.state set to pending unless excluded by flags - Rejected rows are stored in a durable table linked to campaign_id for later operator review, without inserting Contact rows - Upload returns counts for accepted and rejected rows and includes a row index for each rejection - Tests upload a CSV with 10 valid and 2 invalid rows and assert 10 Contact rows exist and exactly 2 rejections are recorded ### Acceptance — REQ-005 - ContactState has an explicit transition function that rejects illegal transitions, including completed back to calling - Eligibility query selects contacts where do_not_call is false, opt_out_at is null, attempts < max_attempts, and next_attempt_at <= now - Time window rules enforce that scheduling only occurs within configured windows, using campaign timezone stored in rules - Retry policy produces next_attempt_at that is inside a future allowed window, or marks not_reachable when max attempts reached - State changes are transactional with Call updates, preventing partial updates on failure - Tests cover incrementing attempts for no_answer and stopping at exactly 5 attempts with final state not_reachable ### Acceptance — REQ-006 - A provider adapter interface defines methods for start_call and verify_webhook_signature, returning provider_call_id on success - Exactly one concrete adapter is registered and selected by config, and missing or unknown provider config fails startup - Starting a call creates a Call row with correlation_id and attempt_number, and updates ContactState.state to calling - Provider API failures map to Call.status failed and ContactState.state failed or pending with next_attempt_at per policy, per explicit mapping - Adapter hides vendor-specific fields from the domain, storing only provider_name and provider_call_id as required - Tests use a fake adapter that simulates success and failure, asserting DB writes and correct state changes ### Acceptance — REQ-007 - Webhook endpoint rejects missing or invalid signatures with 401 and writes an audit event webhook.rejected with correlation_id - Webhook ingestion is idempotent using a deterministic key based on provider_call_id and event_type, preventing double application - Webhook updates Call.status and outcome based on provider payload mapping, and updates ContactState.last_outcome consistently - Duplicate delivery of the same webhook results in one DB state change and one no-op, and does not increment attempt_count twice - Webhook requests include correlation_id propagation, using an existing Call.correlation_id when resolvable - Tests replay the same webhook twice and assert attempt_count and status remain correct after the second request ### Acceptance — REQ-008 - Call flow logic enforces that consent must be captured before any of the 3 questions are recorded as answers - SurveyResponse is created with consent_granted false initially or on refusal, and with consent_timestamp when granted - When consent is refused or opt-out is detected, ContactState becomes refused or excluded, call is ended, and refusal timestamp is stored - When consent is granted and 3 answers are captured, SurveyResponse.completed_at is set and ContactState becomes completed - Scripts versioning is stored via a campaign config hash or snapshot reference saved with the consent decision - Tests cover refusal path and completion path, asserting stored answers count is exactly 3 and state is completed ### Acceptance — REQ-009 - Domain events survey.completed, survey.refused, survey.not_reached are represented as typed payloads with required fields - Writing a final outcome enqueues an outbox record in the same transaction as ContactState and SurveyResponse changes - A publisher worker polls outbox and publishes to SQS with at least once delivery semantics and correlation_id in message attributes - Worker marks outbox records as sent only after successful SQS publish, and retries transient failures with backoff - Consumer for email-trigger events calls an email adapter interface and writes AuditEvent email.sent or email.failed with redacted payload - Tests validate outbox insertion, publishing with a stub SQS client, and idempotent retry behavior on duplicate outbox processing ### Acceptance — REQ-010 - GET /campaigns/{id}/dashboard returns counts and percentages for completed, refused, not_reachable, and total contacts - Dashboard includes attempt distribution summary and provider error counts derived from Call rows - Freshness requirement is met by deriving metrics from DB with caching TTL at most 60 seconds, or by incremental aggregation updated within 60 seconds - GET /campaigns/{id}/contacts returns a paginated list with contact outcome, attempt_count, and last timestamps - GET /campaigns/{id}/contacts/{contact_id} returns attempt history with Call records and timestamps, hiding transcript fields unless permitted - Tests seed mixed states and assert dashboard totals match ContactState rows within ±1 and updates visible after simulated event write ### Acceptance — REQ-011 - GET /campaigns/{id}/export returns 403 for viewer role and writes AuditEvent export.denied with correlation_id - GET /campaigns/{id}/export returns 200 for manager role and streams CSV with required columns contact_id, phone, outcome, attempt_count, timestamps - Completed contacts include answer_1, answer_2, answer_3 columns populated from SurveyResponse, and empty for non-completed outcomes - Export applies redaction rules to payload logs and does not write full phone numbers into audit payload_redacted fields - Every export attempt writes AuditEvent export.requested and export.completed with row count, duration, and correlation_id - Tests cover viewer denied and manager allowed, validating CSV header and at least one completed row includes all 3 answers ### Acceptance — REQ-012 - Next.js UI provides campaign list page showing name, status, language, and last updated time - Campaign create and edit forms enforce required intro, consent, and exactly 3 questions, with validation errors shown inline - Contacts upload page posts multipart CSV and renders accepted and rejected counts plus per-row rejection reasons - Dashboard page shows completed, refused, not_reachable totals and percentages, and refreshes on an interval not exceeding 60 seconds - Export button is disabled or shows a clear error for viewer role, and triggers download for manager role - Frontend tests cover at least one page render, one form submit happy path, and one RBAC-driven export denial UI state ## Dependency Graph (textual) REQ-002 -> REQ-001 REQ-003 -> REQ-001, REQ-002 REQ-004 -> REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003 REQ-005 -> REQ-001, REQ-003, REQ-004 REQ-006 -> REQ-001, REQ-005 REQ-007 -> REQ-002, REQ-006 REQ-008 -> REQ-005, REQ-007 REQ-009 -> REQ-001, REQ-008 REQ-010 -> REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-008 REQ-011 -> REQ-002, REQ-010 REQ-012 -> REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-010, REQ-011 ## Iteration Strategy - **Batch 1 (S, ±1 batch):** REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003 - **Batch 2 (M, ±1 batch):** REQ-004, REQ-005 - **Batch 3 (M, ±1 batch):** REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008 - **Batch 4 (M, ±1 batch):** REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-011 - **Batch 5 (M, ±1 batch):** REQ-012 - **Ordering rationale:** deliver end-to-end campaign setup and data first, then orchestration and webhooks, then events/metrics/export, then UI. ## Test Strategy - **Per REQ unit tests (python):** domain validation, state transitions, idempotency keys, repositories with transactional rollbacks - **Integration tests (python):** FastAPI routes with test DB, CSV upload, export streaming, webhook signature checks - **Worker tests:** outbox publish retry logic with stub SQS client, email adapter stub - **Frontend tests:** page rendering, form validation, API mocking for upload and dashboard, RBAC UI gating - **Batch E2E (optional per environment):** smoke test script calling create campaign, upload contacts, trigger scheduler tick, and verify dashboard/export ## KIT Readiness (per REQ) - **General paths:** `/runs/kit//src` and `/runs/kit//test` - **REQ-001** - root namespace: `app` - src roots: `/runs/kit/REQ-001/src/app/*` - test roots: `/runs/kit/REQ-001/test/*` - KIT-functional: yes - reuse: `app.security`, `app.repo` - KIT-functional: yes - **REQ-004** - root namespace: `app.api.contacts`, `app.domain.contacts`, `app.common.csv` - reuse: `app.repo`, `app.security` - api documentation artifacts path if needed: `/runs/kit/REQ-004/test/api` - KIT-functional: yes - **REQ-005** - root namespace: `app.domain.orchestration`, `app.common.timewindows` - reuse: `app.domain.contacts`, `app.repo` - KIT-functional: yes - **REQ-006** - root namespace: `app.adapters.telephony`, `app.domain.calls` - reuse: `app.domain.orchestration`, `app.observability` - KIT-functional: yes - **REQ-007** - root namespace: `app.api.webhooks`, `app.security.webhooks` - reuse: `app.adapters.telephony`, `app.domain.calls` - KIT-functional: yes - **REQ-008** - root namespace: `app.domain.surveys`, `app.domain.consent` - reuse: `app.domain.calls`, `app.events` - KIT-functional: yes - **REQ-009** - root namespace: `app.events`, `app.worker.outbox`, `app.adapters.email` - reuse: `app.repo`, `app.observability` - KIT-functional: yes - **REQ-010** - root namespace: `app.api.dashboard`, `app.domain.metrics` - reuse: `app.repo`, `app.common.redaction` - KIT-functional: yes - **REQ-011** - root namespace: `app.api.export`, `app.security.rbac`, `app.common.redaction` - reuse: `app.domain.audit`, `app.repo` - api documentation artifacts path if needed: `/runs/kit/REQ-011/test/api` - KIT-functional: yes - **REQ-012** - root namespace: `ui` (Next.js app), with API client module `ui.lib.api` - src roots: `/runs/kit/REQ-012/src/ui/*` - test roots: `/runs/kit/REQ-012/test/*` - KIT-functional: yes ## Notes - Assumption: SQS is the concrete messaging system for Slice-1, matching TECH_CONSTRAINTS profile app-core. - Risk: provider selection impacts webhook payload mapping and latency; mitigation is strict adapter boundary and extensive webhook mapping tests. - Risk: time window rules complexity; mitigation is to implement a minimal rule structure first and validate explicitly, rejecting unknown shapes. - Data minimization: audit payload_redacted must exclude full phone and any transcript content; enforce via a shared redaction helper and tests. are not applicable here, prefer internal PyPI mirror if available - registries: use enterprise approved package indexes, pin allowed libraries fastapi pydantic sqlalchemy - tokens: never log OIDC tokens or provider credentials, read secrets via environment injected from Secrets Manager END_FILE BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/lane-guides/node.md ## Lane Guide — node ### Tools - tests: Vitest or Jest
